BiblicalUsage: Abner the son of Ner is Saul’s captain and the commander of his army. He introduces David to Saul after Goliath falls; he makes Ishbosheth king after Saul’s death and fights David’s men for years; he defects to David and is murdered by Joab at Hebron — a death David mourns and Joab is never forgiven for.
TheologicalSignificance: Abner is the able man on the wrong side, and then on the right side too late — a general who backs the wrong king, sees the truth, and is killed before he can finish crossing over. I believe his story warns me that seeing the truth is not the same as being safe in it, and that a life of fighting for the wrong cause ends in a grave even David weeps over.
